common_findings: All five prefer E041, medium confidence. Both completion and actual interpretive revision are defensible limited contributions. E041 supplies a positive account connecting enacted revision with expressive form and explains a possible aesthetic loss despite voluntary disclosure and greater overall enjoyment. E100 establishes completion versus indefinite extension, but its more demanding nonreturn example expressly leaves aesthetic value unproved. No central fatal error demonstrated; no established historical priority.

remaining_issues.E041: Actual correction must be valuable for work-grounded reasons beyond nonidentity, authenticity or surprise. Informed imagination can preserve much of the value. The experiential versus relational account, reasonable mistaken uptake in Emma/film, and tradeoffs with helpful introductory explanation remain contested. Delay is only a local option-preserving reason, not a general anti-spoiler rule.
remaining_issues.E100: Necessary completion does not establish desirable permanent disappearance. The sculpture changes truthful circumstances without showing aesthetic value beyond scarcity or urgency. The preservation test still needs standards for acceptable alteration and competing interpretations.

coordinator_text_check: No new manuscript revision or empirical audience claim. Earlier full readings and source checks already distinguish the stipulated film and plausible Emma interpretation from a claim about all readers; E100 admits recordings and future performances.
decision: The unanimous comparison supports an E041 advantage on defended value, not automatic admission. E100 remains a coherent narrower contribution, not a refuted text.
